crm_notes:
Summary: Large quant analytics firm evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency risk scoring and embeddings backbone. Wants predictable token economics and strong SLOs for market hours.

Key excerpts / shorthand: 
- 'Need 5ms P95 for short horizon scoring calls during market open' (Lead quant).
- Batch embeddings for nightly index rebuilds — cost sensitive, can tolerate higher latency off-hours.
- Prefers VPC + customer-managed KMS.
- Wants dedicated GPU pool to avoid noisy neighbor variance during peak trading.

Security path: SOC2 in place, asked for ISO27001 roadmap and KMS/HSM diagram. Legal wants explicit overage caps and rollback policy in SLA.

Action items: SE to validate kernel-level perf on quant models (custom attention ops), Pricing to produce 3-tier commit proposal, AE to coordinate procurement timing.
cost_model_summary:
Three committed capacity scenarios produced during workshop (assumptions below). All numbers use average request length = 512 tokens; cache hit assumed 18% for prefix reuse; batching reduces per-token GPU time by 24% on average. GPU cost input: $9,500 per A100-equivalent GPU-month (list price used by finance).

Scenario A — Conservative (Low Utilization):
- Commit: 12 GPUs dedicated
- Assumed utilization for live traffic: 60% (accounting for market pulses, maintenance windows)
- Effective GPU-months utilized: 12 * 0.6 = 7.2
- Monthly commit cost: 12 * $9,500 = $114,000
- Effective per-token cost (monthly): assume 10M tokens/month after batching & cache. Unit cost = $114,000 / 10,000,000 = $0.0114 per token (1.14 cents)

Scenario B — Target (Recommended):
- Commit: 20 GPUs
- Assumed utilization: 80% (target with autoscaling headroom set to burst to public pool)
- Monthly commit cost: 20 * $9,500 = $190,000
- Effective tokens/month: 35M (includes high-throughput scoring + nightly embedding rebuilds)
- Unit cost = $190,000 / 35,000,000 = $0.00543 per token (~0.54 cents)

Scenario C — Aggressive High Util (Cost-Optimal):
- Commit: 36 GPUs (aim to fully host peak load on-reserve)
- Assumed utilization: 92%
- Monthly commit cost: 36 * $9,500 = $342,000
- Effective tokens/month: 120M (heavy throughput scenario)
- Unit cost = $342,000 / 120,000,000 = $0.00285 per token (~0.285 cents)

Notes on assumptions & levers:
- Caching: each additional 5% cache hit reduces token consumption linearly; for their workload, improving prefix reuse from 18% to 30% lowers effective unit cost by ~12% in the target scenario.
- Batching: model-level batching tuning yields 18–30% per-token GPU time reduction; conservative value used here is 24%.
- Burst policy: recommended mix: 80% steady commit, 20% burst to shared pool to keep commit size moderate. Contract should include explicit burst caps and pricing for burst minutes.
- SLA economics: offering a 99.95% uptime SLA with P95 latency targets and credits tied to latency miss windows (not just availability) increases price by ~8–12% in pricing model.
- Overages: propose capped overage rate at 1.5x unit cost above committed baseline; customer pushing for fixed monthly overage ceiling.

Recommendation: Start with Scenario B (20 GPUs) + 20% burst policy, include performance-based credits in SLA but limit maximum credit exposure, add a 6–9 month cadence for commit reevaluation after telemetry-based utilization analysis.
technical_requirements:
- P95 latency target: 5–10ms for short scoring model (512 tokens) during market hours.
- Throughput target: sustained 10k tokens/sec during peak windows, burst to 40k tokens/sec.
- Support for quantized model variants and KV cache sharing within VPC.
- KMS integration for envelope encryption; key rotation policy required.
- Audit logging of token-level access for 12 months.
- Can accept private control plane (preferred) or dedicated-hosted control plane with IP allowlist.
